guarantees.title: Single derived-output runtime timeline
guarantees.claim_summary: Within the named runtime paths, Strategies consume declared signal, context, and metric outputs published by the Indicator timeline, while projection and reporting paths do not become alternate decision semantics.
claim_scope: Indicator-engine publication and Strategy evaluation paths named by the enforcement references.
Representative overlay, runtime-push, and durable-report projection paths at the frozen baseline.
failure_semantics: A generic, projection, or reporting path reconstructs decision semantics outside the published runtime timeline.
A Strategy reads an overlay, detail, lifecycle output, or Indicator-private state as a decision input.
wording_constraints: AGENTS.md is retained only as nonactivating governance context and does not strengthen the platform-contract clauses.
Referenced QT-TERM labels remain unadopted Phase 2A glossary entries.
The repository-wide consumer and reconstruction-path inventory is not closed; the claim is limited to the named paths.

guarantees.title: Exact frozen binding for canonical backtests
guarantees.claim_summary: A canonical backtest represented by the named admission and worker paths binds one Frozen Dataset to the exact Strategy, Indicator graph, execution configuration, instruments, and half-open ranges without runtime substitution or expansion.
claim_scope: Backtest plan derivation, Dataset admission, and worker-scope binding at the frozen baseline.
The exact configuration and range fields represented by backtest_dataset_binding.v1.
failure_semantics: A canonical backtest starts without an admitted Dataset identity.
A worker expands a range or substitutes Dataset, Strategy, Indicator, execution-policy, instrument, or run configuration material.
wording_constraints: Referenced QT-TERM labels remain unadopted Phase 2A glossary entries.
The claim does not imply that every historical run has a verifiable frozen binding.
This accepted-ADR decision is indexed as a nonactivating candidate, not an adopted normative platform promise.

guarantees.title: Dataset reality separated from consumer admission
guarantees.claim_summary: The named freeze path records source, quality, and gap reality, while each named consumer path applies its own explicit admissibility policy without rewriting the frozen evidence.
claim_scope: Frozen Check binding construction and the named Check gap-policy evaluation paths.
Pinned quality and gap evidence represented at the frozen baseline.
failure_semantics: A consumer represents its admissibility decision as a change to frozen source reality.
A Dataset freeze suppresses a known gap solely because one consumer would reject it.
wording_constraints: Accepted ADR 0062 is decision authority but remains nonactivating and does not adopt the proposed glossary.
Coverage and readiness terms must remain qualified under QT-CONFLICT-008 and QT-CONFLICT-014.
The claim does not make one consumer's readiness policy universal across Backtest, Indicator, Check, and reporting boundaries.

guarantees.title: Check verdict authority ceiling
guarantees.claim_summary: A Check result or verdict is bounded analytical evidence and does not by itself grant Strategy, execution, promotion, or scientific-certification authority.
claim_scope: Check result/verdict construction, canonical result-reference validation, and scientific-certificate issuance paths named below.
The authority separation expressed by ADR 0062 and the active Check boundary.
failure_semantics: A Check verdict alone is accepted as a Strategy decision, execution authorization, promotion decision, or scientific certificate.
An adapter or orchestration layer upgrades Check evidence without the separately owned authority artifact.
wording_constraints: Promotion, deployment, and external-order authority remain distinct under QT-CONFLICT-025.
The claim does not deny that a canonical Check reference can be one input to a separately authorized Scientific Protocol.
This is a nonactivating candidate capability ceiling; it does not certify the completeness of every promotion or scientific-authority entrypoint.

guarantees.title: External order submission remains closed
guarantees.claim_summary: In the named simulation and Bot-control paths, a live label or provider credential/capability does not authorize external order submission, which remains closed pending a separate accepted decision and admission boundary.
claim_scope: Current Bot execution-behavior normalization, simulation execution profiles, and guarded run-start paths.
The no-authorized-production-order boundary at frozen baseline d46e40bf.
failure_semantics: A live runtime/lifecycle label selects an external-order adapter.
Provider credentials or supportsOrders metadata alone enable submission, amendment, or cancellation of an external order.
wording_constraints: Live runtime/composition and deployment authority terms remain unadopted and qualified.
The repository-wide absence claim still requires a generated production-code path inventory; named guards are not exhaustive absence proof.
This record does not prohibit simulated fills or separately reviewed future live-trading work.

guarantees.title: Complete Indicator output catalogs and shared Strategy reads
guarantees.claim_summary: The named Indicator catalog and Strategy read paths expose complete preference-free public output catalogs, leave output selection to consumers, and reuse the established compiler and variant resolver for effective and decision-input reads.
claim_scope: Indicator factory metadata and split Strategy read contracts represented by the named enforcement references.
Public output catalog, effective Strategy, and decision-input read behavior at the frozen baseline.
failure_semantics: A split Strategy read reconstructs effective rules or Variant filters outside the shared compiler/resolver.
Persisted Indicator identity or catalog output is changed by UI or consumer output preferences.
wording_constraints: Indicator, output, and Strategy-stage terminology remains unadopted.
The named paths are representative and do not close every Indicator registry or Strategy read entrypoint.
The typed and legacy overlay registries remain distinct and unresolved; neither is treated as redundant.

guarantees.title: Indicator output presence and readiness separation
guarantees.claim_summary: For the named Indicator-engine and validation paths, every declared output is present on every processed bar, while ready=false marks a present output as unavailable to consumers.
claim_scope: Declared-output presence and readiness behavior at the frozen baseline.
IndicatorEngine step validation, RuntimeOutput schema checks, and backend runtime-validation summaries.
failure_semantics: A consumer treats ready=false as usable output or as an implicit wait/substitution instruction.
An Indicator omits a declared output for a processed bar without failing the engine boundary.
wording_constraints: Output readiness is not runtime, reporting, BotLens, comparison, golden, or deployment readiness.
The proof covers the named engine and validation surfaces rather than every registered Indicator implementation dynamically.
Typed Indicator Output and Qualified Readiness remain unadopted glossary entries.

guarantees.title: Indicator engine publication authority
guarantees.claim_summary: The named Indicator engine owns output validation, the Indicator-scoped commit sequence, and typed provenance deltas for its published output truth.
claim_scope: Backend runtime-output evidence for the same published rows at the frozen baseline.
IndicatorEngine construction, per-bar snapshot validation, commit stamping, and output-delta emission.
failure_semantics: A published output bypasses declared-shape, bar-time, dependency, or provenance validation.
An Indicator implementation stamps or advances its own competing publication commit sequence.
wording_constraints: Indicator commit sequence is Indicator-scoped and must not be described as a global cursor.
Indicator output and Qualified Cursor terminology remains unadopted.
The record does not make overlays, details, or lifecycle labels Strategy-visible inputs.

guarantees.title: Projection visibility does not change Indicator truth
guarantees.claim_summary: In the named engine and Strategy paths, overlays, details, debug payloads, and retained history may change visibility but do not change published typed Indicator outputs or Strategy decisions.
claim_scope: Indicator overlay/detail contract separation, bounded overlay projection, and Strategy history represented below.
Output and decision equality across named projection/detail modes at the frozen baseline.
failure_semantics: Enabling, disabling, pruning, or failing an overlay/detail path changes a typed Indicator output.
Overlay, detail, debug, or retained history enters Strategy evaluation as alternate truth.
wording_constraints: A projection failure may degrade visibility and still must remain explicit; nonauthority does not mean healthy or ready.
Overlay and typed-output labels remain unadopted glossary entries.
The active typed and legacy overlay registries remain unresolved and are not consolidated by this classification.

guarantees.title: Indicator lifecycle evidence separated from Strategy inputs
guarantees.claim_summary: In the named Indicator and Strategy paths, lifecycle outputs are typed public Indicator evidence with boundary-validated shapes and are excluded from Strategy-visible signal, context, and metric inputs.
claim_scope: Indicator lifecycle output contracts and the named Strategy evaluator type filters.
Lifecycle rows represented by the backend runtime-output evidence collector at the frozen baseline.
failure_semantics: A lifecycle output with an invalid public shape is published as valid Indicator evidence.
A Strategy consumes a lifecycle output as a trigger, context, or metric input.
wording_constraints: Indicator lifecycle output is not a Bot Run, trade, order, collector, or deployment lifecycle event.
The focused lifecycle proof is partial and shares the broader derived-output boundary with QT-GC-002.
The lifecycle terminology remains an unadopted glossary entry.

guarantees.title: Strategy decision artifacts remain separate from execution
guarantees.claim_summary: In the named Strategy evaluator paths, accepted and rejected decisions are emitted as typed decision artifacts with stable causal identity, while execution remains a separate downstream concern.
claim_scope: Accepted and rejected decision artifacts constructed by the named Strategy evaluator paths at the frozen baseline.
The decision-versus-execution boundary established by accepted ADR 0005 and described by the decision-layer boundary.
failure_semantics: A named evaluator path aliases a Strategy decision to an execution artifact or performs execution as part of decision construction.
An accepted or rejected decision produced by the named paths lacks the stable typed identity or rejection information required by its path-specific contract.
wording_constraints: Accepted ADR 0005 is decision authority but does not activate this guarantee.
Signal, decision, order, and fill terminology remains unadopted and must remain qualified.
The available tests cover representative accepted and rejected paths, not every decision producer or downstream execution consumer.

guarantees.title: Strategy variants remain deterministic public-output filters
guarantees.claim_summary: In the named variant-resolution paths, a Strategy variant is materialized as deterministic filter conditions over public outputs already available to the base Strategy and does not acquire execution-economics or routing ownership.
claim_scope: The ownership exclusions stated by accepted ADR 0018 for at-the-money selection, execution economics, and routing.
Variant validation and filter materialization in the named strategy-variant resolution paths.
failure_semantics: A named variant path accepts a filter over an output outside the compiled public-output catalog.
A variant changes at-the-money selection, execution economics, routing, Indicator configuration, or evaluator ownership.
wording_constraints: Accepted ADR 0018 is decision authority but does not activate this guarantee.
Strategy Variant and Output Filter remain unadopted glossary terms.
The named tests cover representative filter materialization and compile validation, not the complete variant/operator universe.

guarantees.title: Effective Strategy resolution parity
guarantees.claim_summary: In the named preview, Bot, runtime, and provenance paths, effective Strategy configuration and identity are derived through the shared variant-resolution boundary rather than independently reconstructed.
claim_scope: Effective Strategy resolution and stable hash construction in the named resolver and strategy-service call sites.
Preview, Bot, runtime, and provenance parity required by accepted ADR 0018.
failure_semantics: A named consumer independently reconstructs variant semantics instead of using the shared resolution boundary.
The same base Strategy and selected variant resolve to different effective configuration or identity across named consumers.
wording_constraints: Accepted ADR 0018 is decision authority but does not activate this guarantee.
Named call sites and focused tests do not establish a closed inventory of every preview, Bot, runtime, reporting, or provenance consumer.
The stages indexed by the unadopted Strategy glossary entries must remain explicitly qualified.

guarantees.title: Deterministic sequential experiment plans
guarantees.claim_summary: In the named experiment-orchestration paths, an experiment plan is file-backed, canonically hashed, and expanded into a deterministic sequential window-by-variant plan whose declared Strategy variant is verified before execution.
claim_scope: Experiment plan parsing, canonical identity, step expansion, and runner sequencing in the named paths.
The file-backed sequential plan policy established by accepted ADR 0019.
failure_semantics: A step mutates undeclared semantics beyond its window/variant coordinates or executes with a Strategy variant different from the declared plan.
Equivalent plan inputs produce unstable plan identity or step order in the named orchestration paths.
wording_constraints: Accepted ADR 0019 is decision authority but does not activate this guarantee.
Strategy stage terminology remains unadopted and must remain qualified.
The available examples do not yet provide property-level coverage for all plan permutations, resume states, or tampering cases.

decision_reviews.question: Should these well-aligned but unactivated claims remain candidates until their repository-level wording and authority adoption are separately approved?
decision_reviews.draft_judgment: Keep each at candidate. The frozen baseline supplies strong accepted-decision and behavioral evidence, but this classification draft cannot turn that evidence into an adopted repository guarantee.
decision_reviews.blocking_effect: Blocks activation or promotion to enforced; does not block retaining the evidence and proof definitions.

decision_reviews.question: What reviewed denominator closes all causal, projection, reporting, and reconstruction consumers without resolving the existing reconstruction-authority conflicts?
decision_reviews.draft_judgment: Partially enforced for the named paths only. Keep the repository-wide denominator and every authority choice pending under QT-REM-100.
decision_reviews.blocking_effect: Blocks stronger wording, conflict resolution, and activation.

decision_reviews.question: Can execution-runtime and security owners approve a closed repository inventory proving that no unreviewed external-order submission path exists?
decision_reviews.draft_judgment: Partially enforced because direct startup and simulation guards exist, but a reviewed absence proof is missing.
decision_reviews.blocking_effect: Blocks enforced disposition and activation; this review cannot enable external submission.

decision_reviews.question: Do the platform-contract owners confirm these conservatively scoped Indicator claims and approve closed registered-output, projection, publication, and Strategy-read denominators?
decision_reviews.draft_judgment: Partially enforced for the exact named implementation paths. Do not consolidate competing registries, broaden the dynamic denominator, or adopt the deferred Indicator terminology in this batch.
decision_reviews.blocking_effect: Blocks repository-wide wording, registry-authority resolution, terminology adoption, and activation.

decision_reviews.question: Do the decision-layer, execution-runtime, and strategy-service owners approve the producer, filter, and consumer denominators needed to lift the accepted ADR decisions beyond named-path partial enforcement?
decision_reviews.draft_judgment: Partially enforced. Accepted ADRs are primary decision authority, while focused behavior is supporting evidence and neither source activates these guarantees.
decision_reviews.blocking_effect: Blocks stronger disposition, product-semantic changes, terminology adoption, and activation.

decision_reviews.question: What owner-approved property domain and resume/tamper matrix are sufficient to substantiate the full deterministic experiment-plan claim?
decision_reviews.draft_judgment: Partially enforced for the named plan and runner paths. ADR 0019 is decision authority but the examples are not a complete property proof.
decision_reviews.blocking_effect: Blocks enforced disposition, changes to experiment policy or resume behavior, and activation.

decision_reviews.question: Will terminology owners separately adopt, defer, rename, or reject the referenced glossary proposals without treating these classifications as adoption?
decision_reviews.draft_judgment: All referenced terms remain unadopted, including proposed entries. This batch introduces no new term and makes no alias, deprecation, or conflict decision.
decision_reviews.blocking_effect: Blocks terminology adoption and any unqualified wording that depends on the proposed glossary.

notes.message: This narrowed Batch A classifies exactly 14 candidates: QT-GC-002, QT-GC-006, QT-GC-007, QT-GC-010, QT-GC-015, and QT-GC-027 through QT-GC-035. QT-GC-016 through QT-GC-026 were removed from this batch and remain unclassified here.

Accepted ADRs are treated as decision authority but remain nonactivating. Active behavior and tests are evidence only. Source-module contracts and AGENTS.md remain nonactivating. The guarantee registry is nonnormative and every final authority claim remains controlled by its cited source.

QT-PROOF-100 through QT-PROOF-104 and QT-PROOF-116 through QT-PROOF-124 are required-proof definitions only. No selector was executed for this classification draft, no result is asserted, and no attestation is created.

This draft does not activate a guarantee, adopt or resolve terminology, repair product semantics, delete or archive material, choose between normative conflicts, or modify the final registry, proof catalog, glossary, product code, or normative documentation.

Every repository-wide or absence-style claim is intentionally limited to named paths unless a remediation draft supplies an owner-reviewed closed denominator. Existing Phase 1 findings remain attached; an empty new_conflicts array means only that this batch discovered no additional conflict.
